# Three-Pass Critique and Improvements

> Chesed sees every feature, Gevurah tests each claim; Tiferes joins the vessels without making them the same.  
> The Awtsmoos renews both scene and test; Awtsmoos.com must prove the user-facing path, not merely import the rest.

## Pass One — Boundless Improvements

1. Real Canvas preview from the canonical shared movie runtime.
2. Real requestAnimationFrame playback synchronized to movie duration.
3. Frame-accurate scrubbing and selected-scene synchronization.
4. Shared movie JSON loading normalized through procedural core.
5. AI intent compilation from the procedural movie gateway.
6. Procedural asset capability display in Studio.
7. Native procedural asset invocation hooks for renderer-capable surfaces.
8. 2D, 3D, and hybrid capability badges derived from actual profiles.
9. Mobile-first viewport preserving a fixed logical render resolution.
10. Responsive timeline with scene markers and playhead feedback.
11. Scene selection jumps playback to its start.
12. Playback stops exactly at movie duration.
13. Loading a new movie resets stale playback state.
14. Browser console remains clean under load, play, seek, and resize.
15. Reduced-motion UI preference must not break movie timing semantics.
16. Five app adapters declare distinct personalities rather than identical wrappers.
17. Slides receives an adapter if missing.
18. Adapter tests verify projection/roundtrip shape, not only imports.
19. Shared UI compiler gets runtime smoke through the real Studio app.
20. Canonical three-minute movie remains source of truth for proof rendering.
21. Current proof export must be exactly near 180 seconds by ffprobe.
22. Visual diversity must be checked from multiple temporal samples.
23. Current source line-count and tab audits must pass for touched files.
24. Handoff must distinguish native 3D rendering from Canvas fallback semantics.

## Pass Two — Failure Attack

- Decorative viewport risk -> bind actual canvas renderer.
- Fake play risk -> dedicated playback controller with rAF lifecycle.
- Two canonical movie libraries risk -> procedural gateway becomes Studio's single public import gate.
- Render target collision risk -> never take over another session's leased Chrome target.
- Old proof confusion -> write fresh output to a uniquely named completion proof folder.
- Codec instability -> honor the active 30-second stability experiment; inspect its result before launching the long render.
- Mobile jank -> cap rendering work to canonical canvas size and CSS-scale it.
- JSON invalidity -> bridge validates before replacing active project.
- Adapter drift -> shared capability-report test across all five personalities.
- Hidden 3D fallback -> expose native/fallback capability metadata explicitly.

## Pass Three — Final Improvements

1. Reuse the mature shared Canvas renderer rather than inventing a second painter.
2. Keep playback/controller separate from UI action functions.
3. Keep DOM lookup isolated in a viewport binding module.
4. Use named data attributes so browser tests can select controls reliably.
5. Use current canonical `ThreeMinuteMovie` in Studio instead of the weaker 12-scene duplicate if format compatibility permits.
6. Convert only through a tested bridge, never by guessing scene shapes.
7. Split any new source before 120 lines.
8. Do not rewrite dirty legacy roots to add adapters; import adapters independently and verify them.
9. Write fresh proof receipts alongside the final MP4 with ffprobe JSON.
10. Sample at least six timestamps from the final MP4 and compare frame hashes/entropy so a static or frozen movie cannot pass by duration alone.
11. Confirm audio stream presence if browser export promises audio; otherwise document video-only truth.
12. Run all shared movie tests plus Studio, UI, procedural gateway, and adapter smokes after implementation.
13. Re-read every touched file after tests.
14. Re-run git status immediately before final report to avoid attributing concurrent work incorrectly.
15. Keep remaining work non-empty until browser mobile proof and exact media proof both pass.
